title: Skin-Inspired Electronics: An Emerging Sensing and Computing Platform
problem: Current tactile sensing systems lack the dense sensor integration and neuromorphic encoding needed to replicate skin's rich mechanoreceptive capabilities for prosthetic feedback and wearable/implantable applications.
motivation: Prosthetic limbs and wearable devices require seamless sensory feedback (shape, texture, temperature, pain) to enable natural dexterity and user interaction without relying solely on visual cues.
method: Neuromorphic skin-inspired platform integrating highly dense tactile sensor arrays with neuromorphic encoding circuits coupled to a neuromodulator, providing both sensing and signal computing for prosthetics, wearables, and implantables.
key_novelty: Neuromorphic encoding architecture coupled with dense sensor arrays and integrated neuromodulation for brain-machine-like tactile feedback.
contributions: Highly dense tactile sensor array architecture
Neuromorphic signal encoding matching peripheral nervous system processing
Platform design enabling prosthetic, wearable, and implantable applications
primary_theme: neuromorphic tactile sensing for prosthetics and wearables
